anchors_note: Each item carries score anchors for bands 1/3/5 (DI-3): score against these to calibrate across reviews; 2 and 4 interpolate. A score's rationale should name the band it matched.

default.description: Default code review rubric — applied to Stage 3 implementation reviews

items.label: Correctness
items.criteria: Does the implementation do what the spec requires? Are edge cases handled? Input validation present?

anchors.5: Does exactly what the spec requires; edge cases, failure paths, and input validation all handled and verified.
anchors.3: Happy path is correct, but 1-2 edge cases or a failure path are unhandled.
anchors.1: Fails on a known or likely input, or does not meet the stated spec.

items.label: Completeness
items.criteria: Are all specified requirements implemented? No missing features or skipped ACs?

anchors.5: Every specified requirement/AC implemented; no gaps or skipped ACs.
anchors.3: Most requirements implemented; one meaningful gap or skipped AC.
anchors.1: Major features missing; well under the required scope.

items.label: Quality
items.criteria: Is the code well-structured, readable, and maintainable? Follows project patterns? No magic numbers or deep chains?

anchors.5: DRY, readable, pattern-compliant, and tested; no smells, magic numbers, or deep chains.
anchors.3: Works but has duplication, a pattern mismatch, weak naming, or a test gap.
anchors.1: Unmaintainable or unsafe patterns; effectively untested.

documentation.description: Documentation review rubric — applied when reviewing REQUESTS.md, PROGRESS.md, RETROSPECTIVE.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md

items.label: Clarity
items.criteria: Is the document clear, unambiguous, and free of contradictions? Does it use precise language?

anchors.5: Precise, unambiguous, internally consistent; no contradictions.
anchors.3: Mostly clear; a few ambiguous statements or a minor inconsistency.
anchors.1: Ambiguous or self-contradictory; a reader cannot rely on it.

items.label: Completeness
items.criteria: Does the document cover all required sections? Are all FRs/ACs/phases addressed?

anchors.5: All required sections present; every FR/AC/phase addressed.
anchors.3: Most sections present; one required section or several ACs missing.
anchors.1: Major sections missing; key requirements unaddressed.

items.label: Actionability
items.criteria: Can an implementer act on this document without asking follow-up questions? Are file paths, commands, and expected outputs specified?

anchors.5: An implementer can act with zero follow-up; paths, commands, and expected outputs all specified.
anchors.3: Mostly actionable; some paths/commands/outputs missing and a few questions remain.
anchors.1: Not actionable; an implementer must ask many follow-ups.

planning.description: Planning review rubric — applied to PROGRESS.md at S2→S3 AK gate

items.label: Phase Completeness
items.criteria: Every phase has goals, file changes, AC checkboxes, agent assignment, and wave/dependency metadata. 4+ file phases are split into Steps.

anchors.5: Every phase has goals, file changes, testable AC checkboxes, agent assignment, and wave/dependency metadata; 4+ file phases split into Steps.
anchors.3: Phases mostly complete; one phase missing metadata, or an oversized phase not split.
anchors.1: Phases lack goals/ACs/metadata; not executable as written.

items.label: AC Reference Validity
items.criteria: Each phase references at least one AC from REQUESTS.md. AC checkboxes are testable per Spec Granularity Rules (running X produces Y).

anchors.5: Every phase references >=1 REQUESTS AC; all AC checkboxes testable (running X produces Y).
anchors.3: Most phases reference an AC; a few ACs are vague or not testable.
anchors.1: Phases lack AC references, or ACs are not testable.

items.label: Feasibility & File References
items.criteria: File references resolve to existing files (or new files marked Create). Phase dependencies are correctly ordered. Risks are present.

anchors.5: All file refs resolve (or are marked Create); dependencies correctly ordered; risks present.
anchors.3: Mostly feasible; a file ref or two unresolved, or a dependency mis-ordered.
anchors.1: References do not resolve / dependencies wrong; the plan is not executable.
